texts: When a lantern shows mist-light at night, the mist-light attracts nightmoths.
Whenever a lantern shows mist-light at night, the mist-light draws nightmoths.
Nightmoths do not see ordinary firelight.
Nightmoths rarely fly on a cold night.

fields.sentence: When a lantern shows mist-light at night, the mist-light attracts nightmoths.
parse: (: lantern_mistlight_rule (Implication (And (Member $l lantern) (Member $s show) (Agent $s $l) (Theme $s $m) (Member $m mist_light) (Time $s night)) (And (Member (sk_attract $s) attract) (Agent (sk_attract $s) $m) (Theme (sk_attract $s) nightmoth) (During (sk_attract $s) $s))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: Bare "when P, Q" with indefinite participants correctly takes the whenever rule form (Skolem consequent + During, no QuantifierPhrase); roles follow the tests (inanimate transitive subject Agent, unchanged object Theme) and "at night" is the licensed day-part Time symbol. Individuating the mist-light as a premise variable is what lets the anaphoric definite "the mist-light" bind in the consequent.

fields.sentence: Whenever a lantern shows mist-light at night, the mist-light draws nightmoths.
parse: (: lantern_mistlight_draws (Implication (And (Member $e show) (Member $x lantern) (Agent $e $x) (Theme $e mist_light) (Time $e night)) (And (Member (sk_draw $e) draw) (Agent (sk_draw $e) mist_light) (Theme (sk_draw $e) nightmoth) (During (sk_draw $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: Whenever-rule shape (trigger clause as premises, Skolem consequent tied by During, no QuantifierPhrase companion, STV 1.0 0.9) and both compound decompositions (genus light / moth, noun modifiers mist and night correctly unexposed) follow the instruction set. Bare-kind fillers for mist_light and nightmoth, the inanimate transitive Agent, Theme for show/draw, and (Time $e night) as a day-part are all licensed.

fields.sentence: Nightmoths do not see ordinary firelight.

q2_gaps: negated generic whose subject and object are BOTH bare kind-denoting NPs ('Nightmoths' / 'ordinary firelight') — the relational-generic trigger (opaque kind-level relation, non-distributing) and the negated-verbal-generic rule (distributing Implication at strength 0.0) both claim the sentence and no precedence is stated; the 'adjectivally-restricted kind subject forces the distributing-rule route' carve-out is written for the subject only, not for a restricted object

a plain descriptive adjective restricting a BARE mass / kind-level object ('ordinary firelight') — the adjective+noun line bars fusing incidental description, but its split form needs a witness to carry (Member <witness> <prop>), and a kind-level role filler has none, so fusion is the only representable option
review.notes: Follows Negated verbal generic exactly (distributing rule at STV 0.0 0.9, no QuantifierPhrase for plain 'not'), with stative-perception roles Experiencer/Stimulus and the correct solid-compound genus for nightmoth with the noun modifier 'night' left unexposed. Both gaps are about which route the instruction set licenses, not about the atoms emitted.

fields.sentence: Nightmoths rarely fly on a cold night.

q2_gaps: a modified indefinite temporal NP ('on a cold night') as a Time filler: the Time section licenses only structured calendar terms, deictic/named constants and bare day-part symbols, none of which can carry the 'cold' modifier, so putting an sk_ witness (here a per-binding Skolem term) in the Time slot and typing it with Member atoms is unspecified
review.notes: Rare-frequency dial (0.1) plus the 'rarely' QuantifierPhrase companion, the solid-spelling genus night_moth->moth with the noun modifier unexposed, and Agent for self-propelled fly all match the instruction set. The cold-night restriction sits inside the rule's conclusion rather than restricting the occasions, which the VP-scope reading of 'rarely' supports and no rule forbids.
